title: **Why Antagonists Matter**
use_cases: Use when developing a character arc to test hero beliefs
Implement when crafting narrative conflict to drive transformation
Configure when establishing the primary source of resistance in a plot
content:
At their best, antagonists aren’t just roadblocks. They’re forces of change. Whether it’s a corrupt CEO, a best friend turned rival, or even the protagonist’s own inner demons, the antagonist provides resistance that tests the hero’s beliefs, decisions, and transformation.
As we explore in[The Art of Conflict: Character vs. Character in Fiction](https://www.firstediting.com/blogs/character-vs-character-in-fiction/), conflict drives the emotional arc of a story. And often, the most potent source of that conflict is an intelligently crafted antagonist.
